title: Initializer Git Object Identity
purpose: Defines the canonical Git object identity representation used by every initializer record, eliminating independent and contradictory revision-string rules.

normative_requirements.text: A Git object identity shall be a structured representation with exactly two fields: object_format and object_id.
The object_format field shall be a string whose value is the constant "sha1" for Version 1.
When object_format is "sha1", the object_id shall be exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
Abbreviated object IDs are forbidden: every object_id shall be the full required length for its declared format.
Named references (branch names, tag names, symbolic refs) are forbidden as object_id values.

Version 1 of the initializer shall restrict Git object identity to SHA-1 only: object_format must be "sha1" and object_id must be exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Support for SHA-256 is reserved for a future schema version.

A source commit identity shall use the structured representation with object_format "sha1" and the object_id shall resolve directly to a commit object in the source repository via `git rev-parse --verify <object_id>^{commit}`.

A source blob identity shall use the structured representation with object_format "sha1" and the object_id shall resolve directly to a blob object in the source repository via `git rev-parse --verify <object_id>^{blob}`.

A generated Git tree or commit identity shall use the structured representation with object_format "sha1" and the object_id shall be the full-length SHA-1 of the generated Git object in the staged or promoted repository.

Every record in the initializer that stores or transmits a Git object identity shall use the canonical structured representation defined by this specification and shall preserve the exact full object_id value.
